metadata.title: Blow up for the critical gKdV equation III: exotic regimes

extraction_notes.note: Restated copies of the tail definitions, eqs. (1.13)-(1.14) in the strategy section and (A.1)-(A.3) in Appendix A, get no node (none is cited); the Section 2.2 versions DP11/DP12 with (2.14)-(2.16) are kept.

The proof of Theorem 1.1 is split between step (iv) of Section 1.4 (PP2) and one sentence in Section 3.1 (PP6); the proof of Proposition 3.1 runs across Sections 3.1-3.5, so it is split into PP7 (setup by contradiction) and PP11 (topological conclusion), with the intermediate bounds (BS2'), (BS3') as separate claims with their own proofs.

The bootstrap bounds (BS1)-(BS3), (BS2'), (BS3') are \leqno-tagged unnumbered displays cited by name only; they stay inside the proposition and claim nodes, and references to them became hand-added uses edges.
Numbered equation (1.3) is named the sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality with a citation, so it is a theorem (external) rather than an equation.

Uncited standard facts about gKdV (conservation laws, symmetries, global existence below the mass of Q) typed claim with origin external; ClP1 also introduces M and E but is kept a claim rather than a definition.

The strategy section derives the formal dynamics in prose; the decomposition ansatz and the explicit threshold solution are claims, the formal modulation system is a heuristic claim, and the formal integration is a prose proof of ClP6.

The opening sentence 'We now claim from a standard topological argument ...' matches the inline-claim opener, but its argument is the whole remaining section; it is a setup step instead of a parent of every later step.

metadata.extraction_comment: Lemma 2.1 (LP1) is kept origin paper although its part (ii) is quoted from MMR1; Lemma 2.2 (LP2) and the localized virial Lemma B.1 (LP6) are marked external (MMR1) as the paper says it recalls them.

nodes.statement: \ \\ (i) Blow up in finite time: for any nu > frac 1113, there exists u in C((0,T_0],H^1) solution of blowing up at t=0 with \|u_x(t)\|_L^2 sim t^-nu\ \ mboxas\ \ tdownarrow 0^+. (ii) Grow up in infinite time: there exists uin C([T_0,+infty),H^1) solution of growing up at +infty with \|u_x(t)\|_L^2 sim e^t \ \ mboxas\ \ tto +infty. For any nu>0, there exists uin C([0,+infty),H^1) solution of growing up at +infty with \|u_x(t)\|_L^2 sim t^nu\ \ mboxas\ \ tto +infty. Moreover, such solutions can be taken arbitrarily close in H^1 to the family of solitons.

nodes.statement: 1. Sharpness of the results in . Theorem above shows the optimality of the results in since it proves that some decay assumption (such as u_0in mathcal A) is required to obtain a unique stable blow up rate 1/(T-t). This is in contrast with the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, for which the stable blow up rate is obtained in H^1, without additional decay assumption (see and references therein). Note from the proof that the solutions obtained in Theorem are expected to be unstable (except may be for nu<1 in ). Indeed, they are constructed using a topogical argument involving two possible directions of instability.\\
nodes.raw_latex: {\it 1. Sharpness of the results in \cite{MMR1, MMR2}}. Theorem \ref{th:1} above shows the optimality of the results in  \cite{MMR1, MMR2} since it proves that some decay assumption (such as $u_0\in \mathcal A$) is required to obtain a unique  stable blow up rate $1/(T-t)$. This is in contrast with the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, for which the stable blow up rate is obtained in $H^1$, without additional decay assumption (see \cite{MRjams} and references therein). Note from the proof that the solutions obtained in Theorem \ref{th:1} are expected to be unstable (except may be for $\nu<1$ in \eqref{th:1:1}). Indeed, they are constructed using a topogical argument involving two possible directions of instability.\\

nodes.statement: 3. On the role of tails. As one can see from the proof of Theorem , the blow up rate is directly related to the precise behavior of the initial data on the right. In particular, other type of blow up speeds can be produced by similar arguments by adjusting the tail of the initial data. A similar phenomenon was observed for global in time growing up solutions to the parabolic energy critical harmonic heat flow by Gustafson, Nakanishi and Tsai . There an explicit formula on the growth of the solution at infinity is given directly in terms of the initial data which is conceptually very similar to what we observe for (gKdV).

 $$

First, we derive a refined equation for $b_s$, taking the scalar product of equation \eqref{eqofeps} by $Q$ and proceeding as   in \cite{MMR1},  proof of Lemma 2.7.

Recall from \cite{MMR1},
$$(\Psi_b,Q)= -\frac {b^2}{8} \|Q\|_{L^1}^2 + O(|b|^3),\quad  (\Phi_b, Q) = -\frac {b_s}{16} \|Q\|_{L^1}^2 +O(|b|^{10}).
$$
Note also that from direct computations and parity properties
\begin{align*}
&\left|\left( ((\varepsilon+pY_0 + Q_b)^5 - Q_b^5 - p5Q^4 Y_0 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon)_y,Q\right)
- 20 bp((Q^3Y_0 P )_y,Q) \right| \\
&+ \left| \left((\widetilde W)_y,Q\right)-20 bp (( P Q^3)_y,Q)\right|\\
& \lesssim  |b|^3 +|p|^3 + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} 
+ (|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} 
  .
\end{align*}
(See \cite{MMR1} for details on the nonlinear terms in $\varepsilon$.)
Using   \eqref{cl.4bis} and 
the above estimates
we find\begin{align}
&\bigg| b_s + 2b^2  - \frac {16}{(\int Q)^2} \bigg( -  p_s (Y_0,Q)  - \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p 
 (Y_0,\Lambda Q)  \nonumber\\
&  -  bp \left[ 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) \right]
 + c_0 \theta \left(\int Q\right) \lambda^{\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta-1}(s) \bigg)\bigg|\\
& \lesssim |b|^3+  |p|^3 +\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} +(|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} 
 +\frac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p|+\frac {\lambda}{x^3} |p|.\label{eq:bautre}
\end{align}

We claim  the following cancellation
\begin{equation}\label{cancel}
- (Y_0,\Lambda Q) + 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) =0.
\end{equation}
Indeed, 
$L(P')= (LP)' + 20 Q^3 Q' P = \Lambda Q + 20 Q^3 Q' P,$
and so from \eqref{eq:23},
\begin{align*}
& - (Y_0,\Lambda Q) + 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) 
\\ &= - (Y_0,\Lambda Q)-  20 (Y_0+1,PQ^3 Q')\\
& = - (Y_0+1 , L(P')) + \int \Lambda Q = - (L(Y_0+1),P') - \frac 12 \int Q
\\ & = - \int P' -  \frac 12 \int Q  =  P(-\infty) - \frac 12 \int Q =0.
\end{align*}
Thus,
\begin{align*}
& \left| 
 - \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p 
 (Y_0,\Lambda Q) +  bp \left[ 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) \right]
\right|  = 
|p| \left| \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b \right|  |(Y_0,\Lambda Q)|.
\end{align*}

\medskip

Now, from $(Y_0,Q) =- \frac 34 \int Q$ (see   \eqref{YQ}),
  using \eqref{cl.1bis} and \eqref{cl.2bis} we note that 
\begin{align}
& \frac {16}{(\int Q)^2} \bigg( -  p_s (Y_0,Q)+ c_0 \theta \left(\int Q\right) \lambda^{\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta-1}(s) \bigg)\nonumber \\
& =   \frac {12}{(\int Q)} c_0 \lambda^{\frac 12} x^{-\theta}  \left(  \frac 12 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} 
 +\frac \theta 3    \frac {x_s}{x}    \right) +O\left(\frac {\lambda}{x^{3}}| p|\right)  + O\left( \frac {\lambda}{x} |p| \left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right|\right).
    \label{pascancel}
\end{align}
Therefore, 
\begin{align}
&\bigg| b_s + 2b^2 - \frac {4}{(\int Q)} c_0 \lambda^{\frac 12} x^{-\theta}  \left(  \frac 32 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} 
 +  \theta     \frac {x_s}{x}    \right)   \bigg| \nonumber \\
& \lesssim  |b|^3 +|p|^3 + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} 
+ (|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} +
\frac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p| + \frac {\lambda}{x^3} |p|
.\label{eq:b}
\end{align}
 

Now, we prove \eqref{fond}. By direct computation,
$$
\frac d{ds}\left( \frac 4{\left(\int Q\right)}c_0 \theta   \lambda^{-\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta}\right) = - \frac {4}{(\int Q)} c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta}  \left(  \frac 32 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} 
 +  \theta     \frac {x_s}{x}    \right)  
$$
$$
\frac d{ds}\left( \frac b{\lambda^2}\right)
 =   \frac {b_s}{\lambda^2} - 2 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \frac b{\lambda^2}
 =   \frac {b_s}{\lambda^2}  + 2 \frac {b^2}{\lambda^2} - 2 \left( \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} +b\right) \frac b{\lambda^2}.$$
 and \eqref{fond} follows from \eqref{eq:b} and \eqref{eq:2002bis}.

Let $\frac 13 <\beta<\frac {11}{20}$. Then
 $$
 t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \lambda^3(s') ds' \leq 
 10^3 \int_{s_0}^{s} (s')^{-3 \beta} ds'  
 \leq \frac {10^3}  {3\beta-1} \left(s_0^{-3\beta+1}-s^{-3\beta +1}\right)
 <1
 $$
 for $s_0$ large enough. For $\beta = \frac 13$,
 $$
 t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \lambda^3(s') ds' \leq 10^3\, {\rm log}\frac s{s_0} \quad 
 \hbox{so that} \quad s \geq s_0 e^{10^{-3} t}.
 $$
 Thus,
 $$
 x(s) \geq \frac 3{20} s^{\frac 23} \geq \frac 3{20} s_0^{\frac 23} e^{\frac 23 10^{-3} t}\geq 10 t^3 .
 $$
 for $s_0$ large enough.

 $$
 t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \lambda^3(s') ds' \leq \frac {10^3}  {1-3\beta} \left(s^{1-3\beta}-s_0^{1-3\beta}\right)
 $$
so that for $s_0$ large
$$s \geq \left( \frac {(1-3\beta) t}{10^3}+s_0^{1-3\beta}\right)^{\frac 1 {1-3\beta}} \geq 100 t^{\frac {1+\beta}{1-\beta}},
 $$
and
 $$x(s) \geq \frac 3{20} s^{1-\beta} \geq 15  t^{1+\beta}.$$
  Since $x(s) \geq \frac 45 x_0$, we obtain $x(t) >  t^{1+\beta} + \frac 23 x_0$.\\
  The estimate \eqref{BSp} is a consequence of \eqref{cl.1bis} and
 $\frac \beta 2 + (1-\beta) \theta = 1$, so that
 $$ 0< p \lesssim \lambda^{\frac 12 } x^{-\theta} (s) \lesssim
 s^{-\frac \beta 2} s^{-\theta  (1-\beta)} \lesssim \frac 1s.

 The estimates  \eqref{BSlsl}-\eqref{BSfond} are   immediate consequences  of \eqref{eq:2002bis}-\eqref{fond}, 
 \eqref{cl.2tri}, the bootstrap assumptions and the upper bound $\beta<\frac {11}{20}$.

 \end{equation}
 Similarly,
 $$
 F'(s^*)= \left(\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}\right) f(s^*) (s^*)^{\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}-1}
 + f'(s^*) (s^*)^{\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}}.
 $$
 We now estimate $f'(s)$. By direct computations and then \eqref{dl}, \eqref{dx}
 and (BS1)-(BS2), 
 \begin{align*}
 f'(s) &= \frac 12 \frac {\lambda_s}{\lambda} \lambda^{\frac 12} - \frac 2{\int Q}c_0 
   x_s x^{-\theta}  \\
 & = \frac 12 \lambda^{\frac 52} \left[
 \frac b{\lambda^2}  - \frac 4{\int Q} c_0  \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta}\right]
+O\left(s^{-\frac 54-\frac \beta 2}\right) \\
 &= \frac 12 \lambda^{\frac 52} g(s) + O\left(s^{-\frac 54-\frac \beta 2}\right) 
 = O\left(s^{-1  -\frac \beta 2 -\frac 1{5}}\right).
 \end{align*}
 Thus, 
 \begin{equation}\label{fstar}
 F'(s^*)=\left(\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}\right) \frac {F(s^*)} {s^*} + O\left( (s^*)^{-1-\frac 1{10}} \right). 
 \end{equation}

 $$

 \geq \frac 1{10} \frac {H(s^*)}{s^*} + O\left((s^*)^{-1-\frac 1{20}}\right)
 \geq \frac 1{20s^*},
 $$
for $s_0$ large enough.

\medskip

By  standard arguments (see e.g. the proof of Lemma 6 in \cite{MMC}),
the strict outgoing behavior {\rm (\ref{dFdG})} ensures that the map $(\lambda_0,b_0)\in \mathcal D \to s^*(x_0,b_0)$
is continuous.
We  define the continuous maps
\begin{align*}
 \lambda_0(F_0) &= s_0^{-\beta}\left( 1 - F_0 s_0^{-\frac 1{10}} \right)^2
\\
  b_0(F_0,G_0) &= \beta s_0^{-1+\frac \beta 2} \lambda_0^{\frac 12}(F_0 ) \left( 1+ \frac 1\beta G_0 s_0^{\frac 32\beta - \frac 1{5}}  \lambda_0^{\frac 32} (F_0)
   \right)\\
  & = \beta s_0^{-1} \left| 1 - F_0 s_0^{-\frac 1{10}}\right|
  \left( 1+ \frac 1\beta G_0 s_0^{- \frac 1{5}}  \left| 1 - F_0 s_0^{-\frac 1{10}}\right|^3
   \right)
\end{align*}
so that
\begin{align*}
G_0 &= s_0^{1-2 \beta +\frac 1{5}} \left( \frac {b_0}{\lambda_0^2} 
- \frac 4{\int Q} c_0  \lambda_0^{-\frac 32} x_0^{-\theta}\right)\\

+\frac 2{\int Q} c_0 \frac 1{\theta-1} x_0^{-\theta+1} \right).
\end{align*}

Now, consider the continous map
\begin{align*}
\mathcal M \ : \ \   \   \mathcal B_{\mathbb{R}^2}  &\to  \mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2} ,\\
   (F_0,G_0) &\mapsto \left(F(s^*(\lambda_0(F_0),b_0(F_0,G_0))), G(s^*(\lambda_0(F_0),b_0(F_0,G_0)))\right).
\end{align*}
where $\mathcal B_{\mathbb{R}^2}$ and $\mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2} $ are, respectively, the ball and  the sphere of $\mathbb{R}^2$ of radius $1$. For $(F_0,G_0)\in \mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2}$, we have
$\mathcal M(F_0,G_0) = (F_0,G_0)$, in other words, 
$\mathcal M$ is the identity on the sphere
$\mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2}$. The existence of such a continuous map 
$\mathcal M$ is  in contradiction with Brouwer's fixed point theorem. Therefore, there exists $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{estimation}
| \lambda_0 - s_0^{-\beta}| \leq s_0^{-\beta - \frac 1{10}},
\quad |b_0 - \beta s_0^{-1}| \leq s_0^{-1- \frac 1{10}},
\end{equation}
and $s^*(\lambda_0,b_0)=+\infty$. 
In particular (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3) hold on $[s_0,+\infty)$.\\
Finally, \eqref{aa2}, \eqref{aaa2} and \eqref{aaaa2} imply \eqref{sharp}.\\

This concludes the proof of Proposition \ref{PR:BS} and therefore also of Theorem \ref{th:1}.
